html: A mammogram is a low-dose X-ray of the breast. It can show changes, including some cancers, years before a lump could be felt.
Advice varies with age and family history. Ask your care team when you should begin and how often to go.

• Wear a two-piece outfit so you only need to remove your top
  • Leave off deodorant, lotion and powder: they can show up on the image
  • Book a week when your breasts tend to be less sore
  • Bring the name of the place where you had past mammograms
Being asked for more pictures is common and usually doesn't mean cancer. Extra views or an ultrasound often clear things up.

title: Mammogram
abstract: What a mammogram shows, when to start and how to get ready.
